note: sr25519 uses Ristretto255 group with Schnorr signatures and includes a VRF. Unlike Ed25519, sr25519 is non-deterministic (signatures include random nonces). The vector below is from w3f/schnorrkel's `can_verify_know_preaudit_deprecated_message` test; it uses a DEPRECATED pre-audit signature format whose transcript layout differs from modern schnorrkel. The Phase 1.5 audit (see tools/swift-review/PHASE_2_STATUS.md) fixed Swift's transcript to match modern rust-schnorrkel exactly: SigningContext + sign-bytes:context + sign-bytes:message + proto-name:Schnorr-sig + sign:pk + sign:R + sign:c. Verifying this deprecated vector under modern transcripts naturally fails — the test is currently XCTSkip with a Phase K follow-up reference (also blocks `testSignFlowEndToEnd` per the existing diagnostic file's note). A future commit can either (a) implement a separate `verify_simple_preaudit_deprecated` path or (b) replace this vector with a modern-format one generated via metamui-crypto-rust/metamui-sr25519. Note: the `context` field is the actual signing context the upstream test uses (`Substrate node`), not the JSON's previously-incorrect `substrate`.
